clue.text: Agents put me underground with information about daily activities

parts.note: to inter is to bury, so burying me is to inter me
diaries record what happens each day

explanation.surface: Spies are told to go to ground and keep a log of their routines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put me underground' gives INTER ME, burying me; DIARIES follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Intermediaries act on behalf of others, as go-betweens or representatives do.

clue.text: What is required to end fuel distribution

indicators.note: a distribution spreads things around, so the letters of these two words are dealt out anew

explanation.surface: A supply chain manager says the key need is to stop fuel rationing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution' rearranges END FUEL; the surface wants it as the noun fuel distribution.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful, used as a noun, is what is necessary, as in 'do the needful'.

clue.text: Arrive without gratitude but welcome guests

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to enter in is to come in or arrive
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone turns up without saying thanks, yet still plays the host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking. TA is a casual British 'thanks'.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain is to receive visitors as a host.

clue.text: Woman seen in back border appears in upper regions

indicators.note: the woman is found inside the other piece
back tells us to read the border word in reverse

parts.note: a rim is an edge or border
Ida is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A lady spotted at the rear edge turns up somewhere high above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the border word round to MIR, and the woman sits inside it after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Midair is the space well above the ground, the sky overhead.

clue.text: Dickens 6 character surrounded by dull toil

indicators.note: the character is enclosed by the word for dull

parts.note: dry, as in a dry lecture, means dull
Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A figure from Dickens is stuck in tedious labour.
explanation.walkthrough: The '6' is most likely the page's possessive, 'Dickens's character': Barnaby Rudge is a Dickens title hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Drudgery is hard, menial and monotonous work, the same as toil.

clue.text: Sharp as a knife's performance before the start of elevenses

parts.note: what a knife does is make a cut

indicators.note: the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A knife works keenly ahead of a mid-morning snack.
explanation.walkthrough: ELEVENSES is a British mid-morning snack or tea break; only its first letter E is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Acute means keen or pointed, like a sharp mind or sharp pain.

clue.text: Appeal for devilish wisdom

parts.note: an imp is a little devil, mischievous creature
lore is traditional knowledge or wisdom

explanation.surface: Someone appeals for the knowledge of the devil.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to beg or plead for something.

clue.text: They clear the way for anagram setters and such miserable people

indicators.note: the word anagram itself tells us to rearrange the letters of the next word

parts.note: weepers are people who cry, the miserable

explanation.surface: Crossword compilers and gloomy folk sweep obstacles from the path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anagram' rearranges SETTERS into STREETS; 'such' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Street sweepers clean roads, literally clearing the path for traffic.

clue.text: Owners secured benefit of investment

parts.note: to land a deal is to secure it
interest is the return earned on money invested

explanation.surface: Property holders lock in returns on their capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The landed interest is the class of landowners, used as a collective noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The landed interest means the landowning class, those who possess estates.

clue.text: Assisted when Arthur initially followed horses

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the name is used

parts.note: someone who follows the horses gambles on races, so has betted

explanation.surface: Arthur helped out after a day at the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'followed horses' is racing slang for gambling, not trailing them.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to aid or help, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: If penniless the wrongful title-holder would discover someone to lend him money

indicators.note: If sets up a condition: take the penny out of the title-holder and the lender is what is left

parts.note: a usurer lends money at interest
the penny, abbreviated P, is the coin the title-holder would lose

explanation.surface: A pretender to the throne, once broke, finds a moneylender.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: remove the penny from the answer and USURER remains, so P goes into USURER.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurper seizes a title or throne without the right to it.

clue.text: Off-putting when fed up with making a mistake

indicators.note: in a clue up can signal reading a word backwards

parts.note: taken as written
erring is going wrong or making an error

explanation.surface: Being fed up with your errors is discouraging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed up' looks like the idiom, but 'up' turns FED into DEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Deferring is postponing, putting off till later.

clue.text: Call up all right in time

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: eve is evening, a time of day
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A phone call is made at the correct moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to summon a memory or feeling to mind.

clue.text: Unemployed chap, I hear, has a robe

indicators.note: I hear points to a word said aloud

parts.note: a man on the dole, the British term for unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: A jobless man has a gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The dole' is British unemployment benefit, so a man on it is a dole man.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolman is a long Turkish robe open at the front.

clue.text: Crazy for something to eat

explanation.definitionFit: Crackers means mad in slang and is also a crisp biscuit eaten with cheese.

clue.text: Shooting for the irregular forces, sir?

indicators.note: irregular describes the forces in the surface but asks for the letters out of order

explanation.surface: An officer is told about gunfire for guerrilla troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irregular forces' reads as guerrillas, but 'irregular' rearranges FORCES SIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossfire is shooting from two or more directions at once.

clue.text: Gives authority to eastern politicians when they are in debt?

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east
an MP is a Member of Parliament
those who owe money are owers

explanation.surface: Eastern politicians in debt hand out power?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags OWERS, a made-up word for people who owe.
explanation.definitionFit: To empower is to grant authority or power to someone.

clue.text: Cut and call, but it doesn't generally appear on one's card

definitions.text: it doesn't generally appear on one's card

parts.note: a nick is a small cut
to name is to call

explanation.surface: A slash and a summons, but you won't see it on a business card.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: a familiar name is rarely printed on a formal card.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickname is an informal name that friends use but rarely appears in print.

clue.text: Something to eat when the old man goes in to have a conversation with one

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to chat is to talk informally
pa is father, the old man
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Dad drops in for a snack and a chat.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is an Indian unleavened flatbread.

clue.text: Without the sober the trunk is what has a drink

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a bole is a tree trunk
TT stands for teetotal, describing those who never drink

explanation.surface: Lacking abstainers, the body is the one with a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside, not lacking: BOLE wraps TT, the abbreviation for teetotal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle is a container that holds liquid to drink.

clue.text: Means of support for wandering settler

indicators.note: the letters stray from their order like a wanderer

explanation.surface: Funds are needed to sustain a roaming pioneer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame that holds up a table top.

clue.text: Shortage of money on the land

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: d was the abbreviation for the British old penny
earth is land or ground

explanation.surface: Cash runs short on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the symbol for an old British penny, from the Latin denarius.
explanation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity or lack of something.

clue.text: Play a note in a branch of medicine

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat medicine
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A tune is performed in a hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact is to perform or act out a role.

clue.text: Vehicle for dealings

definitions.meaning: to have no ... with is to have no dealings with

explanation.definitionFit: A truck is a lorry, and truck also means trade or dealings.

clue.text: Peers love being muddied and stay too long in bed

indicators.note: something muddied is confused, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Aristocrats in love get dirty and lie in.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversleep is to sleep past the time to get up.

clue.text: Time safe for extinction

parts.note: an era is a period of time
sure means safe, as in a sure bet

explanation.surface: A period of security precedes being wiped out.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasure is wiping out or deletion, a form of obliteration.

clue.text: One enters a list to take part in the celebrations

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a roster is a list of names
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A person signs up to join the festivities.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel noisily.

clue.text: The sticks I have arranged in close association

indicators.note: arranged means put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has put their twigs in a neat bundle.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick as thieves describes people who are close friends or allies.
